profile.campus: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia (Equinix Ashburn campus, Data Center Alley)
profile.reading:
This point is mapped as Equinix's DC17 at an address in the 44700 block of Performance Circle in Ashburn, Virginia, on the same street where Equinix's confirmed DC16 building sits at 44740 Performance Circle. Equinix's own dedicated facility page for DC17, built at the same URL pattern the company uses for DC4, DC6, DC16, and DC22, its Washington D.C. metro colocation URL with the DC number appended, currently returns a not found error rather than a facility profile, and DC17 does not appear among the 15 facilities Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro listing page names and links today, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22. That gap does not by itself mean no building exists at this address. Loudoun County property and OSM survey data both place a real structure here, and Equinix has used sequential DC numbering into the twenties elsewhere on this same campus, so a facility once marketed as DC17, or one built and numbered in sequence but never given its own public marketing page, both remain plausible explanations this entry cannot confirm further from Equinix's current public materials.

Ashburn's status as the center of Data Center Alley predates whatever building now stands at this address. AOL built what is generally regarded as the area's first data center, its Dulles Technology Center, in 1997 to support its dial up internet subscriber base, and the fiber capacity that project pulled into Loudoun County helped seed the cluster of interconnected facilities that followed. Equinix opened its own first Ashburn building, DC1, in the late 1990s, and its second building, DC2, earned a reputation, per Data Center Dynamics, as one of the most connected buildings on earth. Loudoun County's data center corridor has since grown into what Data Center Dynamics describes as roughly 10 million square feet of built space consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of electrical power region wide, a figure covering every operator in the corridor rather than Equinix alone.

Where Equinix does publish current building pages on this campus, such as its DC4, DC6, and DC16 facilities nearby, those pages give concrete square footage, redundancy, and certification detail rather than the placeholder or absent page this entry finds for DC17. This entry treats that absence as a documented research gap rather than evidence the building is inactive or unrelated to Equinix, since Loudoun County's data center inventory routinely includes buildings that operators no longer market individually to new customers.

Every building on this campus, whatever its current marketing status, now also sits inside Virginia's evolving electricity regulatory framework for large power users. The State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates in November 2026 that raise a typical residential bill by about 16 dollars a month, while creating a new GS-5 rate class specifically for data centers, effective January 1, 2027, requiring large demand customers on this campus to sign 14 year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees, according to Inside Climate News's reporting on the commission's decision.

profile.research_note: Re-pass 2026-09-06: material finding. The dedicated DC17 URL previously cited as a live source (.../washington-dc-data-centers/dc17) now returns a 404, confirmed by direct fetch and by trying the alternate ashburn-data-centers URL pattern too (also 404). DC17 is also absent from Equinix's current Washington DC metro listing page, which names 15 other facilities (DC1-6, DC10-16, DC21, DC22) with working individual pages for DC4, DC6, DC16, and DC22 confirmed this same pass. Rewrote the reading to state this plainly as a documented gap rather than repeating the prior claim that Equinix's own website confirms this building's address and IBX facility code, which is no longer true and may never have been accurately sourced. Removed the dead dc17 URL from sources, replaced with the current metro listing page (evidence of the gap) plus the existing DCD source. Removed semicolons, extended past 2200 chars (was 2071). Added campus_power_note and campus_buildings_total=15, identical across all 5 Equinix DC-numbered rows touched this round. Flagging for the coordinator: this row's address should be re-verified against Loudoun County property records if a definitive source becomes available, since Equinix's own current public site no longer supports the DC17 identification beyond street proximity to DC16.
profile.regional_context: Ashburn's Data Center Alley, anchored historically by AOL's 1997 Dulles Technology Center and Equinix's own late-1990s DC1/DC2 buildings, is described as the greatest concentration of data center space on the planet at roughly 10 million square feet, and Equinix's Ashburn campus serves one of the top three internet peering exchange markets on the US East Coast.
profile.campus_power_note: Equinix's own Washington D.C. metro data center listing page currently names and links 15 facilities under one page, DC1 through DC6, DC10 through DC16, DC21, and DC22. Most of those addresses sit in Ashburn, Virginia, though the same listing places DC14 in nearby Manassas, so the group spans more of Loudoun County than Ashburn alone. Equinix does not publish a combined power, IT load, or square footage figure for this group of buildings, and at least one building number that appears in public address and survey data for this same area, DC17, does not currently have an active linked page on Equinix's own site. Figures used in these entries are per building, drawn only from what Equinix itself publishes for that specific address, and are never extrapolated from one building to another.

reading.body:
Equinix's Ashburn campus sits at the center of Data Center Alley, a roughly 10-million-square-foot concentration of interconnected data center space in Loudoun County consuming on the order of 1 gigawatt of power across all operators. The campus comprises 15 named facilities that Equinix lists together on its Washington D.C. metro page, though DC17, mapped at 44710 Performance Circle in Ashburn, does not currently appear on that listing or have an active dedicated facility page. Equinix publishes no combined power, IT load, or square footage figure for the campus as a whole, and no published specifications for DC17 specifically.

The published capacity of Equinix's other Ashburn facilities places this campus 26th by power among all Virginia sites with disclosed figures, and ahead of 305 other mapped data center locations in the state, though most mapped facilities publish no capacity data. Virginia's new GS-5 rate class for large data center demand customers, effective January 1 2027, imposes 14-year minimum contracts with cost coverage guarantees on every building on this campus, raising the capital commitment required to operate here.

DC17's absence from Equinix's current public materials represents a documented research gap rather than evidence of inactivity, since Equinix's Ashburn campus routinely includes buildings no longer marketed individually to new customers, and Loudoun County property records confirm a structure at this address. Any assessment of what this specific location means for AI capacity would require either updated specification data from Equinix or independent verification of the building's current power and operational status.
